C-ASSISTANT-HISTORY-372.Summary: Extend the existing offline AI assistant with durable operator-owned answer history, verified document-version references and source actions, without replacing existing models, FTS, ACL or document storage.
C-ASSISTANT-HISTORY-372.Problem: On main@8d6ec438563fefc52077bcc9058234c72a841bf3, results can be raw and invisible, history is browser-only, and archive citations are not bound to the exact source candidate. Document evidence cannot be opened or downloaded directly from the assistant answer.

Goals.Goal: Persist structured answer, verbatim model response, status, prompt, duration, source references and owner in SQLite schema 32; allow paginated re-open without LLM inference.
Link only to authorized FTS candidates and immutable document versions; re-evaluate ACL on each saved-history read and document GET.
Render raw, invalid-JSON and normal task responses safely with human-readable source cards and canonical open/preview/download actions.
Preserve disabled, failed and interrupted statuses and report any failure to save the answer.
Verify clean install, schema 31 to 32 upgrade, retry, integrity, backup/restore, forced migration failure and desktop/mobile operator UX.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact baseline main 8d6ec438563fefc52077bcc9058234c72a841bf3, release 0.4.12, schema 31; linked issue 372. Existing applied migrations must remain unchanged. Migration 032 is additive and subject to coordination with independent issue 371 before merge.

No second document store, regenerated evidence, external CDN, mandatory cloud/model, or untrusted HTML execution. Found references must originate in authorized retrieval and have a valid source kind and object ID.
Do not store model chain-of-thought, LLM API keys or secrets. Store raw response only, with bounded size and same ACL redaction as the structured answer.

History lists are scoped to current workspace and account. History redaction after source access revocation must not leak response, prompt, raw text, or source snippets. Real-time output must also be authorization-checked.
Original document blobs, SHA-256 and document_version records remain immutable; links can target an earlier version but never cause mutation.
Browser-only history from earlier versions is not silently migrated across accounts because its entries have no owner identity. The local data is retained.
Keep the existing responsive sheet, task modes, document preview and main navigation. Do not duplicate search or introduce new production mocks.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Full multi-turn conversational agent, autonomous writes to plans, official reports or calendar, external sharing or automatic trust in LLM citations.
Separate deployment, version increment, installer change or a release workflow run for this feature PR.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The stream returns a source-linked structured result; failed JSON renders as safe readable text rather than an empty panel, and rejected streams are visible.
History survives page reload and supports 31 or more saved requests, pagination, re-open without model call, user-specific deletion and stable ownership isolation.
Clicking any valid source in an answer opens the app document card, previews when available, opens an original in a new tab and downloads the selected immutable version.
Forged source IDs or protocol references in model output cannot create verified source actions; revocation blocks both history replay and all content routes.
Schema 31 to 32 migration, repeat migration, PRAGMA quick_check, foreign_key_check, backup verification, restore and forced failure rollback preserve existing data.
Desktop/mobile browser checks cover result, history, document actions, fallback, unavailable LLM, XSS and page width; project check, tests, smoke and relevant CI pass.
Implementation remains fully functional without remote dependencies, without changing document-source semantics, and without independent agent claims unsupported by tooling.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: GRACE final lint/scope and targeted project CI prove the change on the exact PR head; schema-risk regression checks prove recovery without rebuilding offline bundles during a feature PR.
